# Introduction

This report turns the normalized trajectories into numbers: a growth rate per well and time
window, and a dose-response curve fitted to those rates.

Time-course fitting runs in two stages. `fit_SE.timecourse()` first collapses each well's log
fold change over a time window into a growth rate, then fits a dose-response curve to the rates
within each window. Both stages are driven by arguments you have to choose — there are no
defaults, because the right windows depend on the experiment.

```{r libraries}
library(qs2)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(gDRutils)
library(gDRcore)
library(gDRplots)


```

```{r get_wd}
wd <- getwd()
for (d in c("plots", "gDR_data", "tables")) {
  dir.create(file.path(wd, d), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
}
se <- qs_read(file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_se_normalized.qs2"))


```

# Choosing the time windows

```{r windows}
periods <- list(early = c(0, 24), late = c(24, 72))
normalization_map <- c(early = "None", late = "early")


```

Two windows are enough here. `early` covers the first day after treatment, where most of these
agents act; `late` covers the following two days, and is normalized against `early` so it
describes what changed after the initial response rather than repeating it.

The upper bound stops at 72 h even though imaging continues to 100 h: by then the untreated
wells approach confluence, and a growth rate measured against a saturating control says more
about the plate than about the drug.

```{r fit}
se_fit <- fit_SE.timecourse(se,
                            periods = periods,
                            normalization_map = normalization_map)
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se_fit)


```

# Growth rates

```{r growth_rates, fig.height=9, fig.width=11}
gr <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(se_fit, "GrowthRates")
# rows are (drug | cell line), columns are the time windows
gr[, DrugName := sub("\\|.*", "", rId)]
gr[, period := cId]

p_gr <- ggplot(gr, aes(Concentration, NormalizedGrowthRate, colour = period)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ DrugName, ncol = 3, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(title = "Normalized growth rate against concentration",
       subtitle = "1 = untreated growth, 0 = complete arrest, below 0 = net cell loss",
       x = expression(Concentration ~ (mu * M)), y = "Normalized growth rate") +
  theme_bw()

ggsave(file.path(wd, "plots", "growth_rate_dose_response.svg"), p_gr,
       width = 11, height = 9, device = "svg")
p_gr


```

# Fitted metrics

```{r metrics}
metrics <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(se_fit, "Metrics")

metrics_tab <- metrics[, .(DrugName = sub("\\|.*", "", rId),
                           period = cId,
                           N_conc,
                           xc50 = signif(xc50, 3),
                           h = signif(h, 3),
                           x_inf = signif(x_inf, 3),
                           x_mean = signif(x_mean, 3),
                           r2 = signif(r2, 3),
                           fit_type)][order(period, DrugName)]
generate_datatable(metrics_tab)

writexl::write_xlsx(metrics_tab, file.path(wd, "tables", "timecourse_metrics.xlsx"))


```

`fit_type` says how each curve was resolved. `DRC3pHillFitModelFixS0` is a real sigmoid fit.
`DRCConstantFitResult` means the F-test could not justify a dose-dependent model — the drug did
not move the growth rate over the concentrations tested in that window.
`DRCInvalidFitResult` means the solver was given enough distinct concentrations, attempted the
fit and failed; the row is kept and labelled rather than dropped.

```{r fit_type_counts}
generate_datatable(dcast(metrics_tab, fit_type ~ period, fun.aggregate = length,
                         value.var = "DrugName"))


```

# A qualitative cross-check against the published metrics

The project also published GR metrics computed by its own MATLAB pipeline
(`raw_data/GRmetrics_1.tsv`). Those come from a **different assay** — an endpoint Hoechst/LDR
readout on fixed cells, not this live-imaging time course — and from a different time window.
They are not a reference against which these numbers can be validated, and the comparison below
is not a parity test.

What it can show is whether the two assays rank the eight drugs the same way and land in the
same range. A disagreement there would be worth investigating; agreement is reassuring without
proving anything.

```{r published_comparison}
published <- fread("raw_data/GRmetrics_1.tsv")

# the file covers four MCF10A variants; keep the one these plates were seeded with,
# per the CellLine column of the plate table
published <- published[CellLine == "MCF10A-H2B-mCh",
                       .(DrugName, GR50_published = GR50, GRmax_published = GRmax)]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(published$DrugName))

ours <- metrics_tab[period == "early", .(DrugName, xc50_gDR = xc50, x_inf_gDR = x_inf)]

comparison <- merge(ours, published, by = "DrugName", all.x = TRUE)
generate_datatable(comparison)


```

```{r rank_comparison, fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
rankable <- comparison[is.finite(xc50_gDR) & is.finite(GR50_published)]

if (nrow(rankable) >= 3L) {
  rho <- cor(rankable$xc50_gDR, rankable$GR50_published, method = "spearman")

  p_rank <- ggplot(rankable, aes(GR50_published, xc50_gDR, label = DrugName)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "#129bb3") +
    geom_text(vjust = -0.8, size = 3) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_y_log10() +
    labs(title = "Potency from two different assays",
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "Spearman rho = %.2f over %d drugs; endpoint Hoechst/LDR against live imaging - not a parity test",
           rho, nrow(rankable)),
         x = expression(Published ~ GR50 ~ (mu * M)),
         y = expression(gDR ~ xc50 ~ ", early window" ~ (mu * M))) +
    theme_bw()

  ggsave(file.path(wd, "plots", "potency_vs_published.svg"), p_rank,
         width = 7, height = 5, device = "svg")
  p_rank
} else {
  cat("Fewer than three drugs have a finite potency estimate in both sources;",
      "a rank comparison would not be meaningful.\n")
}


```

Drugs whose curve did not reach 50% of the untreated growth rate within the tested range have
an infinite `xc50` and drop out of this comparison. That is a property of the concentration
range, not a failure of the fit — and it leaves only four drugs on the plot, few enough that
the rank statistic is indicative at best.

The surviving points sit roughly an order of magnitude above the published GR50 values. That
offset is expected rather than alarming: `xc50` and `GR50` cross different thresholds, the
windows differ, and a five-day live-imaging course and a fixed-cell endpoint measure different
things. The point of the panel is the ordering, not the absolute values.

```{r save_fit}
qs_save(se_fit, file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_se_fitted.qs2"))


```

# Conclusion

Eight drugs, two time windows, growth rates and dose-response metrics for each, from a public
Incucyte export and its published plate map. The fitted object is saved to
`gDR_data/gDR_se_fitted.qs2` and the metrics table to `tables/timecourse_metrics.xlsx`.

The obvious next step for anyone adapting this example is the window choice. `periods` and
`normalization_map` are the two arguments that change the answer most, and they encode a
hypothesis about when the drug acts — worth stating explicitly rather than inheriting from
a template.
